The One who forgives: It is my only function. It is all there is really left to do. I watch this man who sometimes seems to suffer.

I watch him struggle with his ego, and I forgive him. I am the One who forgives. 

And as I forgive this man who seems to suffer, there is a peace that comes in this being.

I am the One who forgives. I am not this man who suffers. I am not this man who struggles. I am the One who forgives this man in all his humanness. I am the One who forgives this frail body. I am the One who forgives you. And who are you? You are not that one who suffers, are you? You are the One who forgives me...No! You are the One who forgives this man who suffers. 

Yes. We are One. Do you see? We are the One who forgives. We are the One who walks in Joy. We are Love.

I want to be a holy man; carry Love inside of me. I want to be a holy man. Forgiveness set me free.

I had a teacher once who told me that I did not have to sit for hours at a time in order for meditation to be effective. Just one, two, three breaths. Can you find your attention for three simple breaths?

Can you give your attention to the breath as if your breath were God? Give your breath the attention that you might give if the Great Soul came and sat right next to you.

Feel every sensation as if it were speaking to you the great mysteries of the Universe.

Do not be afraid of the Silence. Just a few breaths.

Breathing in. Breathing out. There are no distractions. Everything that seems to be a distraction is just a reminder of who you really are; the One who observes the distractions; and deeper still, the One who forgives the distractions; and deeper still, the One who knows no distractions.
